hooks.text: Ice burns on a planet hotter than a pizza oven.
A distant world packs solid ice inside an 800 degree heat.
Thirty-three light-years away sits a scorching planet made of hot ice.

title: The Planet Where Ice Burns
description: Gliese 436 b is an exoplanet where intense gravity forces water into solid hot ice despite 800 degree temperatures.

beats.text: Ice burns on a planet hotter than a pizza oven.
beats.visual: Artist concept of exoplanet Gliese 436 b glowing under a red dwarf star, 2015

beats.text: Orbiting a red dwarf in Leo, this world sits thirty-three light-years away.
beats.visual: Constellation Leo star map highlighting red dwarf star systems, 2020

beats.text: Its surface temperatures soar past eight hundred degrees Fahrenheit.
beats.visual: Infrared telescope view of a scorching exoplanet atmosphere, 2012

beats.text: That extreme heat should instantly boil away any water.
beats.visual: Diagram of water boiling into steam under high heat conditions, 2018

beats.text: Instead, massive planetary gravity crushes that water into solid hot ice.
beats.visual: Crystal structure of high pressure ice VII under extreme force, 2019

beats.text: Even though it is scorching, solid ice burns right on the world.
beats.visual: Artist concept of glowing exoplanet surface with crystalline water ice, 2016

beats.text: Ice burns on this strange exoplanet.
beats.visual: Artist impression of Gliese 436 b exoplanet with glowing tail, 2015

better_than_last: This episode applies the cosmic contradiction hook pattern from ep175 to a planetary-scale weirdness subject while ensuring every beat strictly adheres to the 14-word maximum length rule.
